public_rationale: The claim is that most of NVIDIA's sales sit in warehouses and that most buyers have not earned meaningful revenue from their GPUs. Some evidence points his way. Reports say Amazon took about $5 billion of GB300 racks in August 2026 and staged some at sites without enough power. A public tracker found few Grace Blackwell GPUs deployed against announced plans. But Amazon is one buyer, and NVIDIA sold about $96 billion in a single quarter. The tracker counts announced projects, not shipped units. No source estimates what share of all GPUs sold was uninstalled in September 2026, or how many buyers earn revenue from them. The evidence neither shows nor rules out 'most'.
limitations: The Amazon evidence is secondary reporting of internal documents.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue, if they have turned them on at all, and most of NVIDIA's sales are sitting in warehouses.

statement.excerpt: I need to be more blunt here: the vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue, if they’ve turned them on at all. Most of NVIDIA’s sales are sitting in warehouses, and that is a significant disclosure that NVIDIA should have already been forced to make.

from_speaker: the vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs
have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue, if they've turned them on at all
Most of NVIDIA's sales are sitting in warehouses
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post (September 2026), more than half of the GPUs NVIDIA has sold (by value or units) are in storage and not installed. Also, most GPU-buying companies have not yet earned meaningful revenue from them.

He describes a present state without naming a period. The target period is the most recent window public evidence could cover before the post: from the start of NVIDIA's fiscal Q3 2027 (2026-07-27) to the post date (2026-09-22).
'Sitting in warehouses' is read broadly as purchased but not yet installed and powered, which includes racks staged at sites without power.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence (industry-wide estimates, NVIDIA or customer disclosures) showing that most of NVIDIA's sold GPUs were uninstalled or in storage around September 2026, and that most buyers were not earning meaningful revenue from them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence showing that most NVIDIA GPUs sold were installed and running around September 2026, for example customer disclosures or credible estimates that only a small share sits in staging.

evidence.excerpt: Internal documents dated August 2026 show Amazon was set to take delivery of approximately $5 billion worth of GB300 racks that month.
evidence.locator: section 'Racks arriving faster than the grid can keep up', paragraph 2
evidence.publisher: Crypto Briefing (citing ZeroHedge and Business Insider)
evidence.explanation: Shows that one large buyer staged billions of dollars of NVIDIA racks at sites without power. That fits the claim's direction but covers one company, not most of NVIDIA's sales.

evidence.excerpt: 100,128 Grace Blackwell GPUs (GB200/GB300) had been deployed as of July 1, compared with an announced pipeline of around 1.66 million GPUs
evidence.publisher: Analytics India Magazine (reporting Air Street Capital's State of AI Compute Index)
evidence.explanation: Measures publicly announced projects, many of them not yet shipped, and tracks only publicly disclosed clusters. It cannot show what share of GPUs NVIDIA actually sold sits in storage. The date is also just before the target window.

evidence.excerpt: Revenue was $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially.
evidence.explanation: Sets the scale: NVIDIA sold about $96 billion in one quarter. The Amazon staging figures are small next to this, so they cannot show that most sales are warehoused.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Disclosure by NVIDIA or major buyers of installed versus purchased GPU counts, or a credible industry-wide estimate of the share of shipped GPUs uninstalled around September 2026.
